subject: Medford High School Safety Crisis
overview: The Council held an extended session addressing an urgent safety crisis following a stabbing at Medford High School, approving a consolidated package of resolutions calling for security personnel, mental health resources, and crisis communication reforms after hours of public testimony. The Council also pressed the finance director for overdue financial records and addressed municipal planning, licensing, and infrastructure matters.

items.title: Commendation of Medford High School Football Team
items.summary: Approved a resolution commending the Medford High School football team, head coach John Curley, and staff for their athletic season and community outreach.

items.title: Grant of Location: Groundwater Monitoring Well
items.summary: Approved a petition from Arcadis on behalf of General Electric to install a groundwater monitoring well along Commercial Street near Mystic Valley Parkway.

items.title: Common Victualler License: Four Season Boba Tea
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license for Four Season Boba Tea to operate at 34 Riverside Avenue.

items.title: Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness Project Update
items.summary: Placed on file a presentation by Prevention Outreach Director Penny Funaiole detailing the city's Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness grant, community liaison staffing, and virtual resiliency hub network.

items.title: First-Quarter Financial Update and AP Warrants
items.summary: Referred the first-quarter financial update to the Committee of the Whole and requested that the finance director provide overdue accounts payable warrants and budget reports in digital format.

items.title: Medford High School Safety and Violence Response
items.summary: Approved a consolidated package of resolutions responding to a student stabbing at Medford High School, requesting emergency security guards, improved crisis communication protocols, a youth summit, and urgent funding for mental health and safety personnel. The action followed extensive testimony from school administration, union representatives, educators, parents, and students detailing safety concerns and ongoing bullying.

items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions and Meeting Records
items.summary: Approved resolutions recognizing Hanukkah and congratulating Congresswoman Katherine Clark on her leadership election, and approved the minutes of December 6, 2022.

items.title: Tabled Resolution 22-602
items.summary: Tabled resolution 22-602 until the next regular meeting.

items.title: Private Waste Hauler Permitting Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance establishing permitting and operating standards for private waste haulers to the Subcommittee on Rules and Ordinances.

items.title: State Roadway and Parking Requests to DCR
items.summary: Approved resolutions requesting that the Department of Conservation and Recreation repair 17 streetlights along South Border Road and install no-overnight-parking signage along the Route 16 bypass road.

items.title: Council Rule 12 Amendment
items.summary: Referred a proposed revision to Council Rule 12 governing unfinished business and requests to the administration, along with proposed amendments, to the Subcommittee on Rules and Ordinances.

items.title: Tabled ARPA Presentations
items.summary: Tabled three administration items concerning American Rescue Plan Act project presentations to the next regular meeting.
